fixes.explanation: Four days, baker. John 11:17 says Lazarus had already spent four days in the tomb when Jesus arrived. That's the number the text gives. I think this is a heavy part of the story, so I'll let that number sit.

Seven shows up in a lot of places, so I get the reach. But John 11:17 gives a different number: four days in the tomb. Nothing in this passage mentions seven. Stick with what the text counts, friend, and the story gets clearer.
That's right. Martha heard Jesus was coming and went out to meet Him, but Mary stayed at home. Only one sister goes out at that point. Mary gets there a little later, once Martha calls her aside.

Yes, that's what she says: “But even now I know that God will give You whatever You ask of Him.” Look at those two words after “But,” "even now." Her brother has been in the tomb four days, and she still says it to Jesus's face. I think that's some real nerve.

Yes! Martha says, “I know that he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day.” She's got her answer ready, like a baker who already knows the recipe. She's pointing to the last day. Jesus is about to say something that changes how she hears it.

The text doesn't give that as their guess. It says they supposed she was going to the tomb to mourn there. The temple isn't mentioned anywhere in these verses. They saw how quickly she got up, and they followed her with the tomb in mind (John 11:31).

True! Martha said, “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.” Mary comes, falls at His feet, and says, “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.” Same sentence, word for word. I think those words must have meant a lot to both of them.

Look again, friend. Martha says, “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.” Mary says exactly that when she reaches Jesus. The two sisters said the same words, each when she met Him (John 11:21, 32).

True. Some of them asked, “Could not this man who opened the eyes of the blind also have kept Lazarus from dying?” That's in John 11:37. The text says "some of them," and it comes right after others said, “See how He loved him!”

The text says they did. Some of them asked, “Could not this man who opened the eyes of the blind also have kept Lazarus from dying?” That's in John 11:37. It comes right after the Jews said, “See how He loved him!”
Cave it is. John 11:38 says the tomb was a cave with a stone laid across the entrance. That stone is going to matter in a minute, friend. Keep your eye on it.
Yes, and she doesn't dress it up. Martha, the sister of the dead man, says, “Lord, by now he stinks…” and then, “It has already been four days.” That's a woman who tells it straight.
That's not in the text. What Jesus calls out in a loud voice is, “Lazarus, come out!” It's a command to Lazarus, nothing more. He doesn't say anything about the sisters when He calls.

Not what the text says. The man who had been dead came out with his hands and feet bound in strips of linen. His face was wrapped in a cloth too. So something was binding his hands and feet, and that makes the statement false.
That's not the word. Jesus says, “Unwrap him and let him go…” The man who had been dead came out wrapped in linen. The instruction is about taking off the wrappings.
